title: El favor
goal: Be asked a favour you would rather not do
culture: A flat no is expensive between neighbours, so the language does the work instead. Fíjese que and es que buy you room, déjeme ver is a real answer, and no le prometo is the honest end of it. Saying yes and not turning up would cost far more.

beats.es: Vecino, fíjese que necesito que me cuide la casa el fin de semana.
beats.good: Fíjese que back at him is a stall and a softener at once. It signals that a but is coming without committing you to it yet.

beats.es: Es un ratito nomás. ¿Puede o no puede?
beats.say: Es que voy a estar fuera.
beats.en: It’s just that I’ll be away.
ok: es que voy a estar fuera
beats.good: Es que introduces a reason, and half the time the reason never arrives. It is the most useful two words for declining anything in this country.

beats.es: Ah. ¿Y no puede aunque sea el sábado?
beats.good: Déjeme ver — let me see. It is a real answer here rather than a brush-off, and it is understood as one by both sides.

beats.say: Le aviso, pero no le prometo.
beats.en: I’ll let you know, but I’m not promising.
ok: le aviso pero no le prometo
beats.good: No le prometo is the honest end of it. Saying yes and then not turning up would cost you the street, and this costs you nothing.
